statement: The snapshot families' bounds are derived from the documents' share of the heap (`HeapBudget.documents`, a quarter, shared equally by a process's snapshot sources: half each where the control plane runs beside the pipeline), never set: the entries for documents the store does not hold get a fixed sixteenth of it, as counts of a fixed entry size (`SNP-7`), so ids nobody owns, which a client can name, never shrink what the real documents get; each family's bound for documents is what it holds plus the room left of the rest once both families' resident documents are weighed by an estimate never below what a resident document retains (`DocumentWeight`), counted in documents of its typical weight, which leaves out documents more than eight times the median, so one very heavy document takes its own weight from the room and no more; before a family holds any, the bound assumes a typical document. A bound is never below 64 documents, so a document heavier than the whole share is still served. Housekeeping recomputes the bounds each revalidation pass, so the gauge follows what is resident, and before every eviction pass, so a document is evicted only when what is resident weighs more than the share, never on a bound computed from what was resident before (the first estimate, or a mean taken over a few documents); one very large document arriving into a full share evicts at most its own weight in documents of the typical weight. The burst rule holds a family between eviction passes (`SNP-14`). A host whose bound is below the documents it prewarms still turns ready. `cosec.authorization.snapshot.max-apps`, `max-tenants`, `max-absent-apps` and `max-absent-tenants` fail startup as keys CoSec does not read, saying what replaced them; the startup line says the share and what it comes to at the first estimate, and `cosec.snapshot.bound` carries each bound as it moves.
